findings.title: Confirmed: real players always get render quality 0 (null → 0), a saved value overrides ?lowfx, and the step-down only ratchets one way
findings.problem: src/game.ts:70 runs `Number(localStorage.getItem('circuit-crew-quality'))`. With no key stored that is Number(null) === 0, which passes the `saved===0||saved===1` test, so setQuality(0) runs on every fresh profile. That turns off GTAO and bloom and caps DPR at 1 (src/render/toon.ts:99-101). I measured it with tools/quality2-retake/00-fresh.mjs. Garage on a fresh profile reads quality 0, DPR 1, `_GTAOPass:false,_UnrealBloomPass:false` in three cases: the review's ?manual&fullfx URL, plain ?manual, and the real player URL /?level=garage with no manual flag. Stored '1' gives 1 and stored '2' gives 2 (2 only works because the line ignores it and the renderer default stays at 2). Three side effects make it worse. (a) A stored value overrides the renderer's own low setting. With '1' stored, ?manual and ?manual&lowfx both come up at quality 1 with bloom on (06-lowfx.mjs), so ?lowfx is not honoured. (b) adaptQuality (src/game.ts:392-395) only steps down, saves each step, and returns early at q===0. Nothing in src/ can raise quality again; grep finds no settings control. A player who hits one slow 3 s spell keeps lower quality for good. (c) The step-down isn't needed on this host GPU. 05-fps.mjs ran every room in real time (no ?manual) at quality 2, at DPR 1 and DPR 1.5, for 10 s each: 58–60 fps, draw pass 3–10 ms, and quality never stepped down. So nobody since ac29daf (2026-09-29) has seen the bloom or AO tuning, and every review-5 'fullfx' screenshot except camera-render-*-21-quality2 and the quality2-retake set was taken at quality 0. Several art findings were measured on a render players were never meant to get; see the per-claim findings below.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/quality2-retake/05-fps.mjs (q2 holds 58-60 fps in all 9 rooms at DPR 1 and 1.5)
findings.fix: In src/game.ts:70, treat a missing key as 'use the default' and accept 2, but never override the low setting from ?lowfx or plain ?manual. For example: `const raw=localStorage.getItem('circuit-crew-quality');const low=params.has('lowfx')||(this.manual&&!params.has('fullfx'));if(raw!==null&&!low){const saved=Number(raw);if(saved===0||saved===1||saved===2)this.view.setQuality(saved);}`. Better still, let createRenderer decide the low case and expose it. In adaptQuality (src/game.ts:392-395), add a recovery path: after 20 s at ≥58 fps, step up one level and save it. Also clear the stored value when the build version changes, so a past downgrade doesn't stick. Optionally add a Quality row (Low / Medium / High) to the pause menu.
findings.verify: Add a Playwright test: open /?level=garage in a fresh context, read window.__game.view.getQuality() (or expose it through snapshot()). Expect 2, and expect 0 with ?lowfx even when '1' or '2' is stored. Rerun mockups/review5/tools/quality2-retake/00-fresh.mjs: 'player-url fresh' should print quality 2.
findings.verify_reason: I reproduced this myself. Code: src/game.ts:70 runs Number(localStorage.getItem(...)); for a missing key that is Number(null)===0, which passes `saved===0||saved===1`, so setQuality(0) runs. src/game.ts:392-395 only ever steps quality down and returns early at q===0. grep finds no other caller of setQuality and no settings UI. My script mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap2-quality2-retake/v0.mjs opens each URL in a fresh browser context. /?level=garage, ?manual and ?manual&fullfx all give q 0, DPR 1, GTAO off and bloom off. With '1' stored, ?manual&lowfx gives q 1 with bloom on, so the saved value overrides lowfx. With '2' stored, fullfx gives q 2. I also checked mockups/review5/tools/cap.mjs: it never writes the key, so every review-5 fullfx shot taken without cap2/launch2 was rendered at q0. One point for the fix: making q2 the default turns on findings 1–4 for every player, so those fixes should ship with it or before it. The fix should also not recompute `low` in game.ts; it should read the low flag that createRenderer (src/render/toon.ts:70) already computes, so the two rules can't drift apart.
extra_evidence: src/render/toon.ts:70 (low = lowfx || manual&&!fullfx) and :104 (if(low)setQuality(0)), which game.ts:70 then overrides
mockups/review5/tools/cap.mjs:18-23 (no localStorage write, so fullfx captures ran at q0)
findings.fix_correction: Same intent, cleaner form. Have createRenderer return `low` (or a defaultQuality). In game.ts:70: `const raw=localStorage.getItem(key); if(raw!==null&&!this.view.low){const s=Number(raw); if(s===0||s===1||s===2)this.view.setQuality(s);}`. Add a step-up path to adaptQuality. Ship the bloom fixes from findings 1–4 before or alongside making q2 the real default.

findings.title: At quality 2 the Playground win lamp blooms into a white blob that swallows Pip's head and the lamp shade (gets much worse)
findings.problem: The existing claim (playground-models: glow sprite 3.6× the shade at opacity 0.6; playground-teach: Pip washed into a pale ghost) was measured at quality 0. In a real-solve win at quality 2 (01-room.mjs, same push-in frame with a q0 twin), bloom spreads the lamp's ×3 'hot' shade, its 3 m additive glow sprite at 0.6 opacity and the 10-intensity point lamp into one white mass. It covers the lamp shade and post top, Pip's hat, face and both raised mitts, and the box behind. The bright cable on the floor at the left also blooms. Measured: in the lamp area (x 60–460, y 200–480), pixels above 245 luma are 18.1% at q2 and 2.5% at q0. In Pip's body region, pixels above 240 are 22.5% at q2 and 8.4% at q0, and luma spread (std) falls from 38 to 26, so Pip loses his shading and outline. At q2 the win shot no longer shows Pip celebrating with the lamp: it shows a glare. It breaks DR-66 (a glow sprite never hides Pip or the part being taught) and DR-11 (the win frames Pip with the working machine). Verdict: the claim holds and gets much worse at quality 2.
evidence: src/render/actors.ts:21 (hot multiplies the colour by k, so an HDR value goes over the bloom threshold)
findings.fix: In src/levels/decor.ts:93, drop the shade to hot('#fff0c0',1.4) so it barely crosses the 1.3 threshold. Make the glow sprite glow(game.root,…,1.1,.35), which is ≤1.5× the shade and ≤0.5 opacity per DR-66, and lower the pointLamp intensity to about 5. Alternatively, give the lamp a selective-bloom layer whose bloom strength is ≤.2. Keep the winFocus push-in offset so the lamp is not between the camera and Pip's head.
findings.verify: Rerun node mockups/review5/tools/quality2-retake/01-room.mjs playground 01. On quality2-retake-03-playground-win-push.jpg, the lamp-area pixels above 245 should be under 5%, Pip-region pixels above 240 under 10%, and Pip's hat outline visible.
findings.verify_reason: I looked at both screenshots. In quality2-retake-03-playground-win-push.jpg the lamp shade and post top have dissolved into a white-yellow glare. Pip's hat, face and raised mitts are washed out with their outlines lost, and the bright floor cable at left blooms. In the q0 twin the shade, Pip's hat with its headlamp, his face and his outline all read clearly. The code matches: src/levels/decor.ts:93-94 has hot('#fff0c0',3), a glow sprite of 3 m at .6 opacity, and a pointLamp of intensity 10. src/render/actors.ts:21 multiplies the colour by k. The bloom threshold is 1.3 (src/render/toon.ts:94). The sprite breaks DR-66: .6 opacity is over the .5 cap, it is much larger than 1.5× the shade, and it hides Pip. I did not recompute the pixel percentages, but the visual difference is unambiguous.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/RULES.md:409-416 (DR-66: glow sprites ≤0.5 opacity, ≤1.5× source, never hide Pip)

findings.title: At quality 2 the Meeting win's projector 'light-up' blooms the screen white: the slide and graph that are the payoff disappear
findings.problem: Meeting's lightUp sets the projector screen to a MeshBasicMaterial at colour ×1.25. It also puts a 4 m additive glow sprite at 0.35 opacity in front of the screen, a 7-intensity point lamp, and a 5.1 m beam cone that becomes visible on win. At quality 0 the slide's bars and red trend line read clearly. At quality 2 (same push-in frame) the beam and sprite bloom over the screen's whole left half: the bars and trend line are washed out, the lamp shade at left melts into the glare, and the coworker's head blends into it. Measured on the screen region (x 60–840, y 180–480): pixels above 245 luma are 23.6% at q2 and 9.6% at q0, and contrast std falls from 44.9 to 35.2. Whole-frame blown pixels are 3.94% at q2 and 0.81% at q0. This is not the known 'Pip missing from the win shot' issue (QA 10, meeting-play). Even the machine half of the payoff is unreadable, because the projected slide is the only thing that says 'the meeting can start'. It is a new finding that appears only at quality 2.
findings.fix: In src/levels/decor.ts:169, set the slide colour to setScalar(1.0), so it stays below the 1.3 threshold. Drop the 4 m glow sprite, or shrink it to glow(…,1.2,.25) and place it at the projector lens (12.2, 1.9, −9.8) rather than over the screen. Lower the beam opacity from .14 to .07 and flag it userData.noBloom, or move it to a non-bloom layer. As the general fix, add a selective-bloom layer: render bloom only for meshes tagged as hot emissives (bulbs, arcs, LEDs) and never for screens that carry information.
findings.verify: Rerun 01-room.mjs meeting 07. On quality2-retake-09-meeting-win-push.jpg the screen region should have under 8% blown pixels, the red trend line and the four bars should be visible, and the result should match the q0 twin.
findings.verify_reason: I compared quality2-retake-09-meeting-win-push.jpg with its q0 twin. At q2 the left half to two-thirds of the projector screen is a white glare: the left bars and most of the red trend line are gone, the lamp shade merges into the glare, and the blue coworker's head blends into it. The right-hand bars are still faintly visible, so 'the slide disappears' overstates it slightly, but the payoff is clearly degraded. The code matches: src/levels/decor.ts:169-170 has the slide at ×1.25 MeshBasic, glow(…,4,.35) at z −9.6 in front of the screen, and pointLamp 7. Lines 156-157 have the beam cone at opacity .14, shown on win. The 4 m sprite also breaks DR-66's size cap of 1.5× its source. The fix is sound. Note that ×1.25 on a white texture sits just under the 1.3 threshold, so most of the overflow comes from the additive sprite and beam stacked on top; removing or relocating the sprite is the main lever.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/quality2-retake-09-meeting-win-push.jpg (right bars still faintly visible, left side blown)

findings.title: Garage kickback arc at quality 2 whites out 40% of the bench board and 100% of the switch, against 17% at quality 0 (the 'over 1 s' duration is about 0.6 s)
findings.problem: garage-models and garage-teach report that the arc whites out the switch for over 1 s. I swept the bench view every 0.1 s after PULSE in job 1, at q2 and q0 on the same simulated frame (04-arcsweep.mjs, 44 crops). The arc is visible from +0.8 s to +1.3 s, six frames or about 0.6 s, at both qualities. That shortens the claimed 'over 1 s', but it still breaks DR-79, which limits flashes near a taught part to 120 ms. The extent is much worse at quality 2. Board-crop pixels above 245 luma reach 29–40% at q2 and 11–17% at q0. Over the switch and the ACROSS SWITCH socket they reach 100% at q2 in all six frames, against 55–81% at q0. At q2 the white field spreads across the MOTOR, NODE, SWITCH and CONTROLLER sockets, the scope trace and its 'RESET at shutdown!' caption, the PULSE button and the ACROSS MOTOR / AT CONTROLLER labels. At q0 it is a blob over the switch. The cause is a hot(×3) arc core, a 0.7 m glow sprite at 0.5–1.0 opacity (DR-66 caps it at 0.5), and a point light of 6–16 intensity that flickers on the same board, all fed through bloom. The arc is the failure the job teaches (the kickback spike at the switch), so hiding the switch and the scope at that moment hides the lesson. Verdict: the claim holds on 'whites out the switch', the duration shrinks to about 0.6 s, and it gets worse at quality 2.
findings.fix: In src/stations/garage/station.ts:186-189, use hot('#e8f8ff',1.5) for the core, glow(this.arc,…,.35,.45) for the sprite, and a fixed arcLight intensity of about 3. At :411, clamp the sprite opacity to ≤.5. Keep the arc's bright core under 120 ms: show it at full for 2 frames, then draw it as thin unbloomed blue zig-zags for the rest of arcT. Keep the switch outline and the scope above the effect (renderOrder, or a noBloom layer for the scope's MeshBasic screen).
findings.verify: Rerun node mockups/review5/tools/quality2-retake/04-arcsweep.mjs. Board-crop pixels above 245 should stay under 10% in every frame, the switch crop under 30%, and frames above 20% should number at most 1 (under 120 ms). Check quality2-retake-43-garage-arc-1.0.jpg: the SWITCH label and the scope caption should be readable.
findings.verify_reason: quality2-retake-43-garage-arc-1.0.jpg shows a white field covering the MOTOR, NODE, SWITCH and CONTROLLER sockets and the ACROSS MOTOR, ACROSS SWITCH and AT CONTROLLER labels. The scope's 'RESET at shutdown!' caption is washed out and PULSE is hazed. In the q0 twin the bloom is confined to the switch, and the scope and labels are crisp. The duration correction checks out in code: src/stations/garage/station.ts:390 sets `this.arcT=test?.25:.6`, so the arc lasts 0.6 s (0.25 s for a test pulse), not over 1 s. Both are still far over DR-79's 120 ms flash limit. The rest of the code also matches: :186-189 has arcCore hot(×3) and arcGlow .7 m at .8, and :407-411 has arcLight 6+rand·10 and sprite opacity .5–1.0, which is over the DR-66 cap of .5. I did not rerun the 0.1 s sweep table.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/RULES.md:479-486 (DR-79: flashes near a taught part ≤120 ms)

findings.title: At quality 2 the Arcade LED halo floods the bench monitor (dark screen +75 luma) and the chain, exactly while the player reads LED HEAT
findings.problem: arcade-play and arcade-teach report that the LED halo and bloom cover the monitor during the Claw heat. That was measured at q0, where the halo is a soft green disc over the LED and the monitor stays black. At quality 2 (03-arcade.mjs, claw heating 1.2 s after P, same frame as the q0 twin), bloom spreads the halo (opacity up to .95, station.ts:408) over the whole lower monitor. The LIGHT, LED HEAT and BLOCK HEAT bars and the 'NOT PLAYABLE / FUSE OK' row sit in a white haze, and the monitor bezel glows. On the board, the empty S and D chain slots, the LED and the ACROSS slot turn white. Measured: the monitor's mean luma is 111 at q2 against 36 at q0 (the dark screen lifts by 75 luma), and the bar-area std falls from 68 to 54. Chain/LED-region pixels above 230 are 35.1% at q2 and 7.8% at q0. After the pop, the monitor stays hazed (mean 60 at q2, 20 at q0). This is the moment the player must read LED HEAT and the current to understand 'too much current'. Verdict: the claim holds and gets worse at quality 2.
evidence: src/stations/arcade/station.ts:403-408 (halo opacity min(.95, glowK·.75), scale .4+glowK·.8, ledLight 3·glowK)
findings.fix: In src/stations/arcade/station.ts:408, cap the halo opacity at .45 and its scale at .4+glowK·.4, and set ledLight to ≤1.5. Put the monitor's screen meshes on a no-bloom layer, or render the bench monitor as a DOM or unbloomed overlay, so bloom can't lift its blacks. Show 'over rating' with the LED HEAT bar and a red flicker on the dome, not a bigger halo.
findings.verify: Rerun node mockups/review5/tools/quality2-retake/03-arcade.mjs. On quality2-retake-61-arcade-claw-heating.jpg, the monitor's mean luma (x 510–880, y 150–340) should be ≤50 and the chain/LED pixels above 230 should be ≤12%.
findings.verify_reason: In quality2-retake-61-arcade-claw-heating.jpg the monitor's dark screen is visibly lifted into a grey haze and its bezel glows. The LED, the ACROSS slot and the empty S/D slots are bloomed white, and the right side of the board is washed out. In the q0 twin the screen is black and crisp. The CURRENT, LED HEAT and BLOCK HEAT numbers and bars are still readable at q2, so the harm is to contrast and clarity, not lost information; P2 is right. The code matches: src/stations/arcade/station.ts:408 sets halo opacity min(.95,glowK·.75), which is over the DR-66 cap of .5, scale .4+glowK·.8, and ledLight glowK·3. The halo is created at :171 and the light at :172. I did not recompute the luma figures.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/quality2-retake-61-arcade-claw-heating.jpg: bars and numbers still legible through the haze

findings.title: GTAO at quality 2 re-renders the whole scene: +730–765 draw calls (+63–65%) for a few local contact shadows, and it greys Pip's overalls
findings.problem: Real-time measurement at quality 2 (05-fps.mjs, no ?manual): lobby 1076–1086 draw calls, playground 1203, spectrum 1776–1786, observatory 1791–1807, garage 1906, meeting 1921–1934, qfn 1966, lunch 2045–2070, arcade 2334–2344. Surveys reach 2302–2457 (01-room.mjs: meeting 2310, lunch 2302, arcade 2457). That confirms the camera-render range of 1203–2344, with the arcade survey slightly higher at 2457. Frame rate holds at 58–60 fps on the host GPU even at DPR 1.5, so DR-24 passes on fps and fails on draw calls by 4–10×. The new part is where the extra draws come from. With the same frame at q2 and q1 (07-ao.mjs), the garage game camera drops from 1906 to 1169 draws and the meeting from 1931 to 1167, so GTAO alone costs about 740–765 draws because it re-renders every mesh for its normal/depth pass. Only 58 meshes in src/ carry userData.noAO. What AO buys: on the game camera, a mean darkening of 1.9–3.3 luma, with 7–12% of pixels darker by more than 8 (16% at zoom 9). The darkening is mostly useful contact shadows under chairs and cabinets. It also self-shadows Pip's face and overalls (overalls 136 → 130 luma), which muddies the toon read on the hero. When the quality-0 bug is fixed, every player gets this cost.
evidence: src/render/post.ts:24 (only noAO, sprites and transparent meshes are skipped)
findings.fix: Before shipping quality 2 by default, merge static decor (freeze(decorRoot) already exists, src/game.ts:105) into a few BufferGeometry batches per material, so the AO pass's re-render costs tens of draws, not hundreds. Or feed GTAO from a normal buffer written in the main pass (MRT) instead of a second scene render. Tag Pip's rig meshes userData.noAO, or lower blendIntensity on characters, so the hero stays clean toon. Target: ≤250 draws at q1 and ≤350 at q2 per DR-24.
findings.verify: Rerun 05-fps.mjs and 07-ao.mjs. The q2−q1 draw difference should be ≤50, and the draw totals should meet DR-24. In quality2-retake-71-…-diffmap.png, Pip should show no AO darkening.
findings.verify_reason: I measured it myself with mockups/review5/tools/verify-gap2-quality2-retake/v5.mjs (snap().drawCalls after 1 s, stored quality set before load). Garage reads q2 1906, q1 1169, q0 1156. Meeting reads q2 2054, q1 1280, q0 1267. So GTAO alone adds about 740–775 draws (+63%), which matches the claim. The code matches too: src/render/post.ts:20-24 hides only sprites, noAO meshes and transparent or additive meshes from the AO pass, and only 56 noAO tags exist in src. However, even q0 is 4–5× over DR-24's ~250-draw budget (mockups/review5/RULES.md:167), so GTAO makes an existing failure worse rather than causing it, and fps holds. P2 stands. I did not verify the claim about Pip's overalls greying (136→130 luma). The MRT/normal-buffer suggestion is technically valid but a large change; batching static decor is the more general win.
extra_evidence: verify v5.mjs output: 'garage q 2 draws 1906 / q 1 1169 / q 0 1156; meeting q 2 2054 / q 1 1280 / q 0 1267'
mockups/review5/shots/verify-gap2-quality2-retake-02-garage-start-q2.jpg, verify-gap2-quality2-retake-01-garage-start-q1.jpg (captured, not used for the luma claim)

notes.clarity: Quality 2 hurts clarity where bloom lands on information. The Arcade bench monitor's blacks lift by about 75 luma during the Claw heat. The Garage scope caption and socket labels disappear under the arc. The Meeting projector slide (the only signal that the job worked) washes out. Everywhere else the HUD and world text are the same at both qualities, because the HUD is DOM and the shots are DPR 1 in headless Chromium. All pixel-size claims in other reviews (14 px caps, outline px, marker height) hold at quality 2. The one exception is a real HiDPI display, where quality 0 also caps DPR at 1 instead of 1.5, so in-world signs render softer for players than intended.
notes.fun: Two of the three biggest success moments get worse at quality 2. The Playground lamp turns Pip into a glare blob (lamp-area pixels above 245: 18% at q2, 2.5% at q0), and the Meeting projector slide blooms white. Garage, QFN, Observatory, Spectrum and Lunch win push-ins barely change (whole-frame blown pixels ≈0% at both qualities). Their framing problems from other reviews (Pip cropped, finale out of frame) are camera issues and hold unchanged. Arcade neon banner: mean luma 146 at q2, 145 at q0, with 1.0% vs 0.8% above 230. Bloom doesn't change it, so the arcade-models '8 m glow sprite' finding holds exactly as filed. It is a geometry and opacity issue, not a bloom one.
notes.models: Quality 2 changes nothing about models. AO adds contact shadows under chairs, carts and cabinets, which helps grounding a little: 7–12% of pixels darker by more than 8 luma at the game camera. AO also greys Pip's overalls by about 6 luma. Pip's hat lamp blooms into a slightly larger white dot (217 vs 186 pixels above 248 at zoom 9). That is harmless and not filed. The rim light still does nothing measurable at quality 2. Rim on against ?norim at zoom 9 in the garage gives mean |Δ| 1.29 luma, 1.2% of pixels above 10 (0.54 and 0.43% at q0), so camera-render's 'rim has no effect' claim holds at both qualities.
notes.playability: Quality 2 is affordable on this host: 58–60 fps in all 9 rooms in real time, at DPR 1 and 1.5, with no adaptive step-down in 10 s. Forcing quality 0 on every player therefore gains nothing here. Draw calls at quality 2 are 1076 (lobby) to 2344 (arcade start), and up to 2457 in the arcade survey, against the 250 budget. About 740–765 of each total is the GTAO pass re-drawing the scene. The game.ts:70 bug is confirmed on the real player URL, not only on ?manual. A stored value overrides ?lowfx, and the step-down never recovers, with no settings UI to undo it. DR-54 floor medians are unchanged at quality 2, because AO and bloom don't touch open floor. Lobby: terrazzo 222, rug 206, wood 185. Garage: 223 / 211. QFN wood: 208 / 209. Spectrum tile: 184 / 199. q0 matched within 1. Every DR-54 brightness finding holds as filed.
notes.teaching: The garage arc is the taught failure, and at quality 2 it hides the switch, the node and the scope for the whole visible arc. That is six 0.1 s frames, about 0.6 s, not the 'over 1 s' others reported, and still far over DR-79's 120 ms. At q2 it covers 40% of the board, against 17% at q0. The Arcade LED halo hides LED HEAT and the current bar exactly when 'too much current' is the lesson. The fixes belong in the emissive values (hot ×3, sprite opacity .6–1.0, point lights 6–16) more than in the bloom pass: tune them for quality 2, then confirm quality 0 still reads.

rechecked: camera-render P1 'first-time players always get quality 0': CONFIRMED, including on the real player URL without ?manual. Two new side issues: a stored value overrides ?lowfx, and the downgrade never recovers.

camera-render 'draw calls 1203–2344 at quality 2': CONFIRMED (1076–2344 at start, up to 2457 in the arcade survey). 58–60 fps holds at DPR 1 and 1.5. About 740–765 draws per room come from the GTAO pass alone.
camera-render 'rim light has no measurable effect': HOLDS at quality 2 (mean |Δ| 1.29 luma, 1.2% of pixels >10).
playground-models / playground-teach / characters 'win lamp glow washes Pip': HOLDS and GETS MUCH WORSE at q2 (Pip-region pixels >240: 22.5% vs 8.4%).
arcade-models 'neon glow sprite grows to 8 m': HOLDS unchanged; bloom adds nothing (banner mean 146 vs 145).
arcade-play / arcade-teach 'LED halo covers the monitor at Claw heat': HOLDS and GETS WORSE at q2 (monitor mean 111 vs 36).

garage-models / garage-teach 'arc whites out the switch for over 1 s': whiteout HOLDS and GETS WORSE at q2 (40% vs 17% of the board, switch 100%). Duration CORRECTED to about 0.6 s (+0.8 to +1.3 s) at both qualities.
DR-66 restrained glow: still failing, and failing harder at q2. A new case shows up only at q2: the Meeting projector slide blooms white on win.
DR-54 floor median luma (lobby 185/206/222, garage 211–223, qfn 208–209, spectrum 184–199): HOLDS unchanged at q2 (q0 matched within 1 luma).
Observatory, Spectrum, Lunch, QFN and Garage win push-ins: no bloom whiteout at either quality. Their framing findings are unaffected by quality.
